title: Chronicle
kicker: Quests, failure, memory · history and progression
hook: **Chronicle** is your history — run results, progression, and the lasting sheet of what you earned and spent.

blindSpots.meaning: The history layer (`H`) — ledgers and run memory. Not the Almanac dossier browser.
Nothing you earn disappears with the level. There is no hard ceiling that says the grind is over.
Tracks summoner, plant types, zombie types, and specimens — separate from the souls bank.
A recorded outcome of play — part of history, not a quest checklist.

alsoTrue: Souls buy summons and rituals; XP grows power curves and unlocks — different stocks of progress.
New worlds keep who you are — chronicle memory hangs with that prestige of place.

sections.title: What it is
paras: Your history of the war: what you ran, what you earned, what leveled.
It is the ledger of your summoner story — not a wiki of species art.

rows: Individual demons from work they did — lawn, expedition, battle

cards.name: Progression dossier
cards.body: The lasting sheet of earned and spent power.

groups.title: Chronicle layer (`H`)
groups.intro: Open from the rail when available.
steps: Read run history and XP ledgers.
Cross-check Almanac (`A`) when you want dossiers instead of ledgers.
groups.note: Presentation polish continues; the surface exists in this build.

doSteps: Finish a lawn match or expedition that can grant XP.
Open Chronicle (`H`) and find a ledger that moved.
Note that souls did not replace XP — both can rise for different jobs.
doNote: Stop when chronicle ≠ almanac. Prestige of place: [new world](new-world-prestige).

mixUps.a: No. Quest log is Vision. Chronicle is history and XP.

mixUps.q: Do I lose XP when a world ends?
mixUps.a: You keep who you are — progression banks with the summoner. Loam and map holdings do not.
No hard ceiling — magnitudes keep meaning as you climb.
No. Souls are a separate stock from XP ledgers.
